text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- A message of the Greek Prime Minister's thoughts: Gerassimos Arsenis leaves the National Defence Ministry.
- European Union ambassador to Cyprus Giles Anouil warns that the island's entry to the EU is questionable without a solution to Cyprus problem.
- The participation of the Liberals party in the merger of the left wing Adisok with the centre-left Free Democrats party looks unlikely.
CYPRUS MAIL
- President Glafcos Clerides stresses the need for Turkey to change its position on the Cyprus issue to open the road for a solution.
- Plan is submitted to save threatened buffer zone houses.
- Interpol is called to trace man who kidnapped epileptic son from the UK.
- British Aids woman had an abortion when she learned she was dying, says friend.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Bounced cheques went up by 50 percent in August.
- Cyprus Popular Bank is to promote Fidelity Funds.
- Leading business figure urges government to table legislation enabling the creation of mutual funds to give the stock market a boost.
- Trade deficit rises to 529.1 million pounds.
HARAVGHI
- Simitis' new government is a combination of experience and renewal.
- Money and action is needed to stop 40 buildings from collapsing in the buffer zone.
- Some countries may not endorse Cyprus's accession to the EU if the Cyprus issue is not solved, warns EU ambassador to Cyprus.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- The United Nations have made representations to the government over new armaments of the National Guard.
- Chances of an agreement on cost of living allowance pay between employers and unions appears distant.
- Some government subsidies will have to be scrapped to align legislation with Europe.
SIMERINI
- European Union countries may attempt to bloc Cyprus's accession until after a solution to the Cyprus problem, warns the EU ambassador in Cyprus.
- The university will organise its own entrance exams.
